title: Domain registrars with APIs: comparison data
about: Every datum is a claim: {value, source, checked, note}. value null means not stated: the field could not be sourced from the vendor's own public pages on the checked date. Prices are as the vendor displayed them on that date, in the vendor's currency, and may be promotional; they are strings so nothing is rounded or converted. Pages were read without opening any account.

auth_style.value: Bearer API token in the Authorization header, token needs Registrar write permission; Cloudflare API v4 base URL. Prerequisites: account ID, billing profile with default payment method, default registrant contact, Domain Registration Agreement accepted in the dashboard.

sandbox.note: The Registrar API page does not mention a sandbox or test environment.

whois_privacy.value: Free personal-data redaction, 'if permitted by the registry'. Whether on by default is not stated on the WHOIS page; the overview says redacted WHOIS is offered by default. Registrant state/country stay visible.

dnssec.value: Supported, free, one-click in dashboard. For domains delegated to Cloudflare, Cloudflare publishes CDS/CDNSKEY and Registrar scans them and submits DS to the registry automatically (1 to 2 days).

bulk_reseller.note: No reseller programme found on the pages read. Docs say bulk transfers follow the same process as single ones, each charged individually.

other_notes.value: Transfer-in needs: domain at least 60 days old, no registrant change in 60 days, unlocked, DNSSEC disabled at old registrar, and Cloudflare must be the authoritative DNS (full setup); you cannot use another DNS provider while registered with Cloudflare. Transferred domains locked 60 days. Most gTLD transfers add one year; .uk adds none. Some registrars (Shopify, Block) block nameserver changes so need a workaround. Transfers into Cloudflare are by dashboard; API cannot transfer.

price_notes.value: Annual increments, per domain per year. No volume discounts. Promotional credits cannot be used for domain fees. Registrations and renewals are non-refundable.

whois_privacy.value: Enabled by default on registration and transfer, no separate charge mentioned. Not available for all TLDs. Note: Amazon Registrar hides all contact info; Gandi (registrar associate for some TLDs) hides all except organisation name. .eu not supported; .uk family needs a support case to enable.

dnssec.value: Supported for registration of .com, .uk, .eu and others: you add the public key (KSK/ZSK, base64) via console or API; up to 13 keys for .com/.net, 4 for others. Route 53 can also sign hosted zones. No automatic DS publication described on the page read: you add keys yourself.

bulk_reseller.note: No reseller programme found. Default quota 20 domains per account (increase on request); console transfer-in handles up to five domains at a time.

other_notes.value: Domains are registered via Amazon Registrar or its associate Gandi depending on TLD. Transfer-in: 60-day rule, unlock, no pendingTransfer or similar statuses, disable DNSSEC at old registrar and wait 24 hours. Owner contact changes are ignored during ccTLD transfers. Most gTLD transfers add a year; .uk, .co.uk, .me.uk, .org.uk do not. Domain registered in us-east-1 region only. Domains usually deleted on account closure.

dnssec.value: Supported. With LiveDNS nameservers, activation is automatic from the Nameservers tab ('Go to DNSSEC'), including DS handling at the registry; with external nameservers you submit the public key manually. ALIAS record on the bare domain breaks DNSSEC. API also exposes dnskeys and LiveDNS DNSSEC activation. Docs pages are old; check live panel.
